description: Executable counterpart to the prose `quality.rules` declared in tests/eval/contracts/. Every assertion id here matches a rule id in the corresponding data contract. BigQuery assertions are single-value SQL probes (one row, one numeric column aliased `value`) compared against operator/threshold; the Cloud Bigtable contract cannot be probed with SQL, so its assertions are declarative SDK checks executed against a bounded row scan. Executed by tests/eval/scripts/validate_contracts.py.

conventions.sql_result: Exactly one row, one numeric column aliased `value`.
conventions.ratio_form: COUNTIF(<predicate>) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) so the threshold reads as a pass fraction.

assertions.description: The agent's default `business_date = CURRENT_DATE()` filter must return data while the streaming pipeline is running.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.pos_transactions_gold` WHERE business_date = CURRENT_DATE()

assertions.description: Gold-tier sales totals are never negative.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(total >= 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.pos_transactions_gold`

assertions.description: The scalar item_count agrees with the repeated items record.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(item_count = ARRAY_LENGTH(items)) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.pos_transactions_gold`

assertions.description: alert_type is restricted to the two documented model outputs.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(alert_type IN ('order_anomaly','cashier_promo_abuse')) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.pos_anomaly_alerts`

assertions.description: order_anomaly pairs with order_anomaly_model; cashier_promo_abuse pairs with cashier_abuse_model.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF((alert_type = 'order_anomaly' AND alert_source = 'order_anomaly_model') OR (alert_type = 'cashier_promo_abuse' AND alert_source = 'cashier_abuse_model')) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.pos_anomaly_alerts`

assertions.description: risk_score is a positive-class probability in [0.0, 1.0].
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(risk_score BETWEEN 0.0 AND 1.0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.pos_anomaly_alerts`

assertions.description: The agent's default 7-day cashier_promo_abuse offender ranking must return a non-empty result.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.pos_anomaly_alerts` WHERE alert_type = 'cashier_promo_abuse' AND alert_ts >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)

assertions.description: est_cover_hours_remaining is present and non-negative, so the `< 20.0` stockout-risk filter is well defined.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(est_cover_hours_remaining IS NOT NULL AND est_cover_hours_remaining >= 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.gold_inventory_reconciliation_ledger`

assertions.description: Only the three bands emitted by the reconciliation pipeline occur. The literal values written by the PySpark job are 'CRITICAL BURN SPIKE - STOCKOUT RISK' (Critical), 'MONITOR VELOCITY' (Monitor) and 'RECONCILED NORMAL HEALTH' (Normal), matching the 51 / 84 / 8,265 distribution verified in the Module 1 Lab 1 parity benchmark.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(reconciliation_status IN ('CRITICAL BURN SPIKE - STOCKOUT RISK','MONITOR VELOCITY','RECONCILED NORMAL HEALTH')) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.gold_inventory_reconciliation_ledger`

assertions.description: One reconciled position per (business_date, store_id, item_id).
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(CAST(business_date AS STRING), '|', store_id, '|', item_id)) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.gold_inventory_reconciliation_ledger`

assertions.description: shelf_qty, backroom_qty and opening_qty are all non-negative.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(shelf_qty >= 0 AND backroom_qty >= 0 AND opening_qty >= 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.gold_inventory_reconciliation_ledger`

assertions.description: Every transaction carries at least one line item, so warranty triage UNNEST joins never silently drop transactions.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(ARRAY_LENGTH(items) >= 1) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.historical_transactional_data`

assertions.description: The UC 2.1 warranty triage join key convention holds across clouds: item.item_id values do resolve against warranty_generic_sections_extracted.product_id. Measured as the number of distinct item_ids that join; a value of 0 would mean the join key convention has drifted and every warranty answer would silently report 'uncovered'.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT item.item_id) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.historical_transactional_data` tx, UNNEST(tx.items) AS item JOIN `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted` warr ON item.item_id = warr.product_id
SELECT COUNTIF(transaction_id IS NOT NULL) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.historical_transactional_data`
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT transaction_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(transaction_id),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.historical_transactional_data`

assertions.description: business_date is the DAY partitioning key.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(business_date IS NOT NULL) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.historical_transactional_data`
SELECT COUNTIF(total_amount_usd >= 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.historical_transactional_data`
SELECT COUNTIF(item_count = ARRAY_LENGTH(items)) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal_gold.historical_transactional_data`
SELECT COUNTIF(product_id IS NOT NULL) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted`

assertions.description: One warranty policy row per product, so the UC 2.1 join cannot fan out.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(product_id),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted`
SELECT COUNTIF(product_name IS NOT NULL AND product_name != '') / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted`
SELECT COUNTIF(retail_price_usd IS NOT NULL AND retail_price_usd > 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted`

assertions.description: warranty_duration_months drives the DATE_DIFF coverage decision, so a NULL or non-positive value would silently deny valid claims.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(warranty_duration_months IS NOT NULL AND warranty_duration_months > 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted`

assertions.description: Lab 2b quality gate: every extracted certificate retains at least 800 verbatim characters for grounding.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(LENGTH(extracted_full_content) >= 800) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted`

assertions.description: Extracted row count equals the number of warranty certificate PDFs exposed by the object table, so no PDF was dropped by AI.GENERATE_TABLE.
assertions.sql: SELECT CAST((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted`) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_pdfs_objects`) AS INT64) AS value

assertions.description: Every source_pdf_uri points at an object present in the warranty_generic_pdfs_objects object table.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(warr.source_pdf_uri IN (SELECT obj.uri FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_pdfs_objects` obj)) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.module1_unstructureddata.warranty_generic_sections_extracted` warr

assertions.description: A bounded SELECT against the federated AWS S3 Iceberg table returns without a BigLake catalog or Iceberg metadata error, confirming the cross-cloud binding is live at query time.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM (SELECT transaction_id FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal-lakehouse.elevate_data.silver_pos_transactions` LIMIT 10)

assertions.description: No checkout escapes the UC 2.3 cross-cloud cashier audit.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(cashier_id IS NOT NULL) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal-lakehouse.elevate_data.silver_pos_transactions`

assertions.description: event_timestamp is a STRING in the Iceberg source; every value must SAFE_CAST to TIMESTAMP so ORDER BY event_timestamp is chronologically meaningful.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(SAFE_CAST(event_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP) IS NOT NULL) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal-lakehouse.elevate_data.silver_pos_transactions`

assertions.description: cashier_id follows the same CASH_#### convention used by pos_anomaly_alerts, so the UC 2.3 Step 1 -> Step 2 handoff joins without normalisation.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNTIF(REGEXP_CONTAINS(cashier_id, r'^CASH_[0-9]+$')) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal-lakehouse.elevate_data.silver_pos_transactions`
SELECT COUNTIF(transaction_id IS NOT NULL) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal-lakehouse.elevate_data.silver_pos_transactions`
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT transaction_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(transaction_id),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal-lakehouse.elevate_data.silver_pos_transactions`
SELECT COUNTIF(total_amount_usd >= 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM `pj-elevate-da.cymbal-lakehouse.elevate_data.silver_pos_transactions`

scan.comment: Default bounded scan used by assertions that do not declare their own row_key_prefix. Bigtable has no SQL surface, so coverage is a bounded row sample rather than a full-table aggregate.

preconditions.description: The UC 1.3 / UC 2.2 target cashier position must be present, otherwise every live-data eval case degrades to 'cashier offline' and the benchmark stops exercising the Bigtable path.

assertions.description: Row keys follow STORE_<3 digits>#CASH_<digits>#<reversed timestamp>; the agent tool builds this key with f"STORE_{int(n):03d}" / f"CASH_{n}".
Stored as a fraction and rendered as a percentage by the agent tool.
Every returned row carries the qualifiers the agent renders, so no metric silently falls back to the tool's 0.0 / 0 / 'unknown' placeholder.

A prefix scan returns the most recent event first. Bigtable scans lexicographically, so this holds only if every reversed-timestamp suffix under the prefix is written with the same digit width and decreases monotonically with recency.
